findings.function: queueBatch, queueAddChain, queueAddRemotePool, queueRemoveRemotePool, queueSetRemoteToken, queueApplyAllowListUpdates (all via _queueAction)
findings.source: ConfigTimelockBatchQueue.sol:100-103 address destination = _configDestination(action_); if (destination == address(0)) revert IConfigTimelockBatchQueue_ConfigDestinationZero(actionId_, index_);
findings.issue: The destination is an immutable that reads as 0, so after validating the first sub-action every queue function reverts with ConfigDestinationZero(actionId, 0); the key loop (:122), _queuedConfigKeyCount (:265), both _queueAction loops (:206, :226), the storage of the action and its events are dead in this bytecode (not counted as source loops).

findings.decompiled: while 2 * _110 > idx: address(stor[idx + sha3(sha3(_param1, 3) + 2)]) = 0; ... idx = idx + 2 / mem[_183 + 64] = stor5[_param1][s][2 * t] / stor5[_param1][s][idx] = 0; stor5[_param1][s][idx + 1] = 0
findings.source: delete of QueuedAction.actions (array of 2-slot BatchAction structs with a bytes member) and of QueuedConfigState[] (2-slot structs)
findings.issue: Arrays of 2-slot structs are indexed by raw slot (2 * t, idx + 1) instead of element and member, and the actions array of a mapping element is addressed as stor[idx + sha3(sha3(_param1, 3) + 2)].
findings.rule: When an array's index is always scaled by the element size k (k * i + c, c < k), print element i, member c (stor5[k1][k2][i].field_c); sha3(sha3(k, m) + c) is the data of the array member at offset c of mapping m's element k.

summary: Complete and faithful; the live source loops are while loops. In this bytecode an immutable destination of 0 makes every queue function revert after validating the first sub-action, so most of the queueing logic is (correctly) absent; the rest is verbose unoptimized code with raw struct-array slot indexing.
